title: Order of Destruction
goal: Ensure values drop in the exact sequence expected by callers.
hints: By default, `_b` drops before `_a`, resulting in 21.
To make `_a` drop first, transfer its ownership early.
explanation: `_b` normally drops before `_a` because local variables are destroyed in reverse declaration order. Calling `std::mem::drop(_a)` forces `_a` to drop first (appending 1), and then `_b` drops at the scope boundary (appending 2) to produce 12. Leaving `()` or dropping `_b` early both result in 21, which fails the expectation.
